o: Build a double round-robin (each ordered pair plays once) with one match per day and no team playing on consecutive days. Total matches = n(n−1). n = 2 or 3 are impossible (too few teams to separate matches involving the same pair/team) → return []. For n ≥ 4: generate single round-robin rounds with the circle method (adding a dummy bye for odd n); within a round each team plays at most once, and distinct rounds are edge-disjoint matchings. Concatenate all rounds, then append the reversed (home/away swapped) rounds, fixing any day-boundary conflict by swapping the first two matches of a round.
k: Circle method produces rounds that are perfect matchings — no team appears twice within a round, so intra-round ordering is always safe.
Conflicts can only occur at round boundaries (last match of one round vs first of the next); swapping the first two matches of the incoming round resolves it since matchings are disjoint.
n ≤ 3 has no valid schedule; n ≥ 4 always does.

a.n: Approach 1: Circle Method Rounds + Boundary Repair
a.i: Generate the standard round-robin rounds (dummy team for odd n), emit each round's matches as consecutive days, then repeat with reversed directions. Before appending a round, if its first match shares a team with the previous day's match, swap its first two matches (every round for n ≥ 4 has ≥ 2 matches).
s: Run the circle method for m−1 rounds (m = n, or n+1 with a None/dummy for odd n), collecting non-bye matches per round.
Flatten rounds into the schedule; at each boundary, swap the incoming round's first two matches if they clash with the previous match.
Append the same rounds with home/away swapped, applying the same boundary repair.
a.t: O(n²) — n(n−1)/2 matches generated with constant work each.

w: The impossibility cases (n = 2, 3) and the boundary-repair trick are the crux; the circle method handles the rest. Any valid schedule is accepted, so minor variations in ordering are fine as long as no team appears on consecutive days — always self-check your output against that invariant. Follow-up: minimize total days with multiple matches per day, or add rest-day constraints.
